_about: The Tidebreak ring (RingArena, RingWater, RingLevel; docs/bending_design.md 'Pro-bending', the plan's T3). Every number here, tunable by eye. The long axis is the arena's local X: side 0 at -X, side 1 at +X. s is metres back from the centre into a side. Zones read from the deck's own build, no painted or lit lines (the owner, 2026-10-04): each zone's deck is laid in its own stone or wood.

looks._about: How each part of the deck is laid: kind stone (cut slabs, slab_m square, a little uneven) or boards (planks plank_w wide running along grain x or z, board_m long, joints staggered); tint multiplies the material's own colour; jitter the slab-to-slab or plank-to-plank tint spread.

sockets._about: Stone sockets in the deck (open rules too): a stone sits in each for Shove, Gust lift and the cushion to work on; taken away, another rises refill_s later; RingArena.rebuild puts every one back. [s, z] per side, mirrored. None since 2026-10-10 (the owner: "remove the boulders in the arenas now"): no stone, no iron collar, in every format; the old places were [[5.0, 5.6], [5.0, -5.6]] (2v2 [[6.0, 7.5], [11.0, 3.0]], 4v4 [[6.0, 10.5], [13.5, 4.0]]: formats' sockets_at). A stone Shove kicks up and every other stone on the deck keep these hurls.
sockets._hurl: A stone on the deck shoved or lifted (a socket's cannonball, a dropped spike, a kicked-up stone: any flight with the open world's moves.json gust.stone.hurl numbers; RingArena._ring_hurls) flies with these by its kind instead: knock-back ammo, not the open world's 45-110 blows (KITS round 2's soak: earth won on shoved cannonballs). A Stone Form cast and a caught stone sent back keep their own.

water._about: The tank's water (RiverWater's shader, river.gdshader, its own material): the colour of 2 m of clear water over a stone floor, a slow drift, no ice.

surround._about: What stands round the tank: a flagged walk (plaza_side m along the long sides, plaza_end m past the ends) at the deck's height, timber stands of tiers along both long sides, and a stone wall across each end, so the eye stays in the arena.

formats._about: The team formats' decks (docs/tidebreak/team_formats_and_arenas.md; the owner, 2026-10-10: 2v2 and 4v4 "we need arenas built big enough"): merged over the base and the rule set's overlay (modes.stock) when MatchSetup's format is one of these (RingArena.set_format); 1v1 is the base. deck_l = neutral_m + 2 x zones x zone_m. slot_z: the spawn line's places across the deck, the player's side's slot 0 his; spout_z: the respawn grates on each end's s line_s(zones - 1), one per fighter of a side; grate_z: every grate line's grates (spout_z among them); sockets.at [s, z] per side. layout: the team arena's raised pieces (RingArena THE LAYOUT; the owner's pick 2026-10-10, 'C · Ruins': a perch with its stairs on each team's flank, broken walls for cover, a broken column, the centre open; each piece also built turned half round the middle), checked against the spawns, grates, spouts and sockets (none within 1 m).

2v2._size: 16 x 34 since 2026-10-12 (the owner: "the zones and 2v2 should have a smaller arena"; was 20 x 40, zone_m 6): the Ruins drawn in to fit, every piece at least 0.3 m off a grate and 2 m off a spawn; the spawns 1 m clear of the grates (at 3 m a ground wave reaching a bot on its spawn ran into a grate's edge)

zones._about: Zones' deck (rule set zones, over stock; a team format's numbers over these): smaller than Lives' (the owner, 2026-10-12: "the zones and 2v2 should have a smaller arena"), 12 x 28, three zones of 4 m a side, the territory fought over closer

modes._about: Overlays on the numbers above for a rule set (RingArena.set_mode: the ring's rule set, RingRules.pick_rule_set). A key here replaces the base's; a block (coping, lanterns, piers, curtain) is the overlay's own. classic has none: today's numbers.

stock._about: The % ring's stage (smash_r3 spec v2 §5.1-5.2): the deck where it is, the water 6 m under it in a deep tank 10 m wide on every side, the deck on piers with a stone face (grabbable), no ropes, the tank's edge a curtain of falling water from a rim channel curtain_up_m over the deck (touching it is touching water: out), a pale stone coping along the four lips (proud for the eye, its collider flush) and lanterns on pier heads just outside the lip. A wall (key 4) stands at least wall_lip_clear_m inside every lip. Respawn spouts on the s 12 m line at spout_z.

arenas._about: The arenas (the owner, 2026-10-16: 'build a new and better arena with a headless blender ... like earth not the wood ... closer to the water maybe a oval shape'; his pick: 'ruin and crater'). The match setup's Arena choice (MatchSetup.arena; RingArena.set_arena): an arena's numbers go over the rule set's and the format's, like modes.stock. classic: today's stone deck in its deep tank, built by RingArena itself. The others are built in Blender by tools/environment/arena/arena_build.py (our own procedural materials baked to textures, nothing third party) and loaded as a mesh (`mesh`, with %s the deck's size: 14x34, 12x28); RingArena keeps every collider and rule and skips its own kit visuals. shape oval: the deck's lip is the ellipse of deck_l x deck_w (on_deck, is_out, nearest_lip, wall_place_ok, the bots' clamps all read it); the zones still run along X. water_y: the deck 2 m over the water ('closer to the water'), out_drop_m with it: a body that far under the deck's top is in the water and out. dressing: the parts of RingDressing kept (the stands' awnings and piers, the gatehouses, the deck's brass trim and caustics are the classic deck's; the lanterns are the arena's own when it has braziers).
